hospitals.description: Children's Hospital of Philadelphia is the freestanding flagship of one of the largest pediatric systems in the country, sitting on Civic Center Boulevard in University City next to Penn Medicine and the University of Pennsylvania. It runs a Level I pediatric trauma center, a Level IV NICU of roughly 95 beds, a full pediatric ED and essentially every pediatric subspecialty, and it trains residents and fellows through Penn's Perelman School of Medicine. The campus keeps growing, with a research tower on Schuylkill Avenue, a 2024 behavioral health crisis center and a new inpatient tower planned for later in the decade. For an acute care PNP it is one of the biggest single employers of pediatric NPs on the East Coast, with inpatient, ICU, surgical and ED teams. The neighborhood is dense and urban, with most staff commuting from the city, the Main Line or South Jersey.
highlights: Consistently ranked among the top 10 U.S. News children's hospitals since 2009
Level I pediatric trauma center and Level IV NICU (about 95 NICU beds)
Penn Perelman teaching hospital with large residency and fellowship programs
Ranked No. 1 nationally in pediatric diabetes and endocrinology and orthopedics (2024-2025)
Second inpatient hospital in King of Prussia since 2022; satellite NICUs at partner hospitals
New 24-story main campus tower planned by about 2028

hospitals.description: CHOP's King of Prussia Hospital, branded the Middleman Family Pavilion, is the system's second inpatient children's hospital and opened in January 2022 off Goddard Boulevard in Montgomery County. The 250,000 square foot building has 52 private rooms split between 36 medical-surgical beds and a 16 bed PICU, plus a pediatric emergency department and a small surgical suite for orthopedic, plastic surgery and ENT cases needing an overnight stay. It connects to CHOP's existing specialty and urgent care center on the same campus. The suburban setting near the King of Prussia mall and the Turnpike makes it a very different commute from University City, and staff often rotate between the two hospitals. Shell space was built in for future growth.
highlights: Opened January 26, 2022 as CHOP's second inpatient hospital
16 bed PICU and 36 medical-surgical beds, all private rooms
Built with shell space; expansion toward about 108 beds has been discussed
Suburban Main Line and Route 422 corridor location
hospitals.notes: Listed separately from the Philadelphia campus because it is a licensed hospital with its own PICU, inpatient units and ED (52 licensed beds on the PA list). hospitals.description: St. Christopher's Hospital for Children is a freestanding pediatric hospital at Erie Avenue and Front Street in North Philadelphia, serving one of the most Medicaid-dependent pediatric populations in the country. It holds Level I pediatric trauma status, runs a Level IV NICU and a pediatric burn center, and trains Drexel and Temple residents. Tower Health and Drexel bought it out of the Hahnemann bankruptcy in 2019 and run it as a joint venture; in 2026 Jefferson, Temple, PCOM and CHOP pledged a combined 30 million dollars to help keep it stable. Finances remain tight, and in 2026 it cut about 60 positions and ended its small kidney transplant program. For a PNP it offers high-acuity, safety-net pediatrics with a strong community health mission.
highlights: One of four Level I pediatric trauma centers in Pennsylvania
Level IV NICU and a pediatric burn center
About 85 percent of patients on Medicaid, the highest share of any U.S. children's hospital per Drexel
30 million dollar support pledge from Jefferson, Temple, PCOM and CHOP (2026)
Teaching site for Drexel and Temple medical schools
hospitals.notes: Financial stability is a real question for a job seeker: 2026 brought roughly 60 position cuts (about half reassigned) and the end of pediatric kidney transplant, though FY2025 showed a small operating profit thanks to city Medicaid funding. Wikipedia infobox lists 189 beds (body says 188). Magnet per Wikipedia (2009); current status not confirmed.
